# Source/generated boundary test only covers Markdown surfaces

## Goal

Extend the source/generated boundary guarantee so a generated file that is not
Markdown cannot sit under `templates/` undetected.

## Background

`tests/test_generate.py::test_no_generated_file_lives_under_templates` (added in
0.68.3) walks `templates/` and fails on any file containing
`gen.DO_NOT_EDIT_MARKER`. That marker is an HTML comment:

```
<!-- Generated by .github/scripts/generate-skill-surfaces.py; do not edit. -->
```

It is therefore only expressible in Markdown. The walk is already
`rglob("*.md")`, so widening the glob alone buys nothing: a generated `.json`
or `.toml` under `templates/` carries no marker in any syntax and would pass
either way. The gap is in the *signal*, not in the traversal.

This was raised as a low-severity finding during the PR #199 review and
rebutted there on that reasoning — closing it properly needs a per-format
marker convention, which is design work rather than a one-line test change.

## Requirements

- Every format `generate-skill-surfaces.py` can emit carries a machine-checkable
  do-not-edit signal, or is covered by an equivalent guarantee.
- The boundary test enumerates from the filesystem, as it does today, rather
  than checking a hard-coded list of paths — a future generator that starts
  writing a new format under `templates/` must fail the test without anyone
  remembering to update it.

## Design questions for the planning phase

- Per-format markers: a `_generated` key for JSON, a comment line for TOML.
  Each needs a writer and a reader.
- Or invert it: assert that the generator's declared output paths are all under
  `generated/`, so the guarantee comes from the writer set rather than from
  scanning content. Likely cheaper and stronger, and composes with the existing
  `GENERATED_REFERENCE_WRITERS` check.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A test proves a non-Markdown generated file placed under `templates/` is
      detected. It must fail against today's code.
- [ ] The chosen convention is documented in the directory-structure spec beside
      the existing "no generator output under `templates/`" rule.
